nodes.name: Candidate set of models $\mathsf{M}_n$
nodes.statement: Suppose further that one wants to conduct inference on $\mathbb{P}_n$, and intends to use as a working model an element of $\mathsf{M}_n$, a set consisting of $d$ nonempty sets of distributions $\mathbb{M}_{1,n}, \hdots,\mathbb{M}_{d,n}$ on the Borel sets of $\R^{n \times \ell}$. Throughout $d$ is fixed, i.e., does not depend on $n$. We emphasize that it is \textit{not} assumed that $\mathbb{P}_n$ is contained in one of the sets $\mathbb{M}_{j,n}$ for $j = 1, \hdots, d$. That is, the candidate set $\mathsf{M}_n$ might be \textit{misspecified}.
nodes.genus: a set consisting of $d$ nonempty sets of distributions
differentia: Throughout $d$ is fixed, i.e., does not depend on $n$
it is \textit{not} assumed that $\mathbb{P}_n$ is contained in one of the sets $\mathbb{M}_{j,n}$

nodes.name: Model-specific target of inference $\theta^*_{\mathbb{M},n}$
nodes.statement: For each model $\mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ one has to define a corresponding target of inference $\theta^*_{\mathbb{M},n} = \theta^*_{\mathbb{M},n}(\mathbb{P}_n)$, say, which we take as given throughout the present section. Furthermore we assume that for every $\mathbb{M}_{j,n} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ the target is an element of a Euclidean space of finite dimension $m(\mathbb{M}_{j,n})$ which does not depend on $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Each candidate model carries its own finite-dimensional target parameter, taken as given.
nodes.genus: an element of a Euclidean space of finite dimension $m(\mathbb{M}_{j,n})$

nodes.name: Model selection procedure $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$
nodes.statement: We take a model selection procedure as given, and denote the model selection procedure used by $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n: \R^{n \times \ell} \to \mathsf{M}_n$ (measurable). That is, the quantity $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n(y)$ denotes the selected model upon observing $y$. We also assume that for every model $\mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ an estimator $\hat{\theta}_{\mathbb{M},n}: \R^{n \times \ell} \to \R^{m(\mathbb{M})}$ (measurable) of the corresponding target $\theta^*_{\mathbb{M},n}$ is available.

nodes.name: Construction of confidence intervals valid post-model-selection
nodes.statement: In this article we address the question how valid confidence intervals can be constructed for the coordinates of the target $\theta^*_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n,n}$. Our approach is as follows: \begin{enumerate} \item Given $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, we construct confidence intervals $\mathrm{\mathrm{CI}}^{(j)}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}$ for the $j$-th component $\theta_{\mathbb{M}, n}^{*(j)}$ of $\theta_{\mathbb{M}, n}^{*}$, for every $j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M})$ and every $\mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ so that \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{P}_n\left( \theta^{*(j)}_{\mathbb{M}, n} \in \mathrm{CI}^{(j)}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}} \text{ for all } j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M}) \text{ and all } \mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n \right) \end{equation*} is not smaller than $1-\alpha$. \item For a model selection procedure $\hat{\M}_n$, our suggested confidence intervals are then obtained via \begin{equation*} \mathrm{\mathrm{CI}}^{(j)}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n} \text{ for } j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n). \end{equation*} From the coverage property in Part~1 we obtain \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{P}_n\left( \theta^{*(j)}_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n} \in \mathrm{CI}^{(j)}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n} \text{ for all } j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation*} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Build per-model CIs with simultaneous asymptotic coverage $1-\alpha$, then plug in the selected model.

nodes.name: POSI constant $K_{1-\alpha}(\Gamma)$
nodes.statement: For $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and a covariance matrix $\Gamma$ we denote by $K_{1-\alpha}(\Gamma)$ the $1-\alpha$-quantile of the distribution of the supremum-norm $\|Z\|_{\infty}$ of $Z \sim N(0, \Gamma)$.
nodes.genus: the $1-\alpha$-quantile of the distribution of the supremum-norm $\|Z\|_{\infty}$

nodes.name: Correlation matrix $\corr(\Sigma)$
nodes.statement: The correlation matrix corresponding to a covariance matrix $\Sigma$ is denoted by $\corr(\Sigma) = \diag(\Sigma)^{\dagger/2} \Sigma \diag(\Sigma)^{\dagger/2}$, where $\diag(\Sigma)$ denotes the diagonal matrix obtained from $\Sigma$ by setting all off-diagonal elements equal to $0$, $A^{\dagger}$ denotes the Moore-Penrose inverse of the quadratic matrix $A$, $A^{1/2}$ denotes the symmetric non-negative definite square root of the non-negative definite matrix $A$, and where we abbreviate $[A^{\dagger}]^{1/2}$ by $A^{\dagger/2}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\corr(\Sigma)$ is $\Sigma$ rescaled by the pseudo-inverse square roots of its diagonal.
nodes.genus: The correlation matrix corresponding to a covariance matrix $\Sigma$

nodes.name: Stacked estimator $\hat{\theta}_n$, stacked target $\theta_n^*$ and dimension $k$
nodes.statement: Our methods for constructing uniformly valid confidence intervals post-model-selection are developed under a high-level condition imposed on the stacked vector of estimators $\hat{\theta}_n = (\hat{\theta}_{\mathbb{M}_1, n}', \hdots, \hat{\theta}_{\mathbb{M}_d, n}')'$ centered at the corresponding stacked vector of targets $\theta_n^* = (\theta^{*'}_{\mathbb{M}_1, n}, \hdots, \theta^{*'}_{\mathbb{M}_d, n})'$. In this section we denote the dimension of $\hat{\theta}_n$ by $$k \quad := \quad \sum_{j = 1}^d m(\mathbb{M}_{j,n}),$$
nodes.statement_short: Stack all model-specific estimators and targets into one $k$-vector, $k=\sum_j m(\mathbb{M}_{j,n})$.

nodes.name: Condition 1 (linear representation of the estimation error)
nodes.statement: There exist Borel measurable functions $g_{i,n}: \R^{1 \times \ell}\to \R^k$ for $i = 1, \hdots, n$, and $\Delta_n:\R^{n\times \ell}\to\R^k$, possibly depending on $\theta^*_n$, so that for $y\in\R^{n\times \ell}$ \begin{equation} \hat{\theta}_n(y) - \theta_n^* \quad = \quad \sum_{i = 1}^n g_{i,n}(y_i) + \Delta_n(y), \end{equation} where, writing $r_n(y) := \sum_{i = 1}^n g_{i,n}(y_i)$, it holds for every $i \in \{1, \hdots, n\}$ and every $j \in \{1, \hdots, k\}$ that \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}_{i,n}\left(g^{(j)}_{i,n}\right) = 0 \quad \text{ and } \quad 0 < \mathbb{V}_{n}\left(r_n^{(j)} \right) < \infty. \end{equation} Furthermore, for every coordinate $j \in \{1, \hdots, k\}$ we have \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbb{V}_n^{-1}\left(r^{(j)}_n\right)\sum_{i = 1}^n \int_{\R^{1 \times \ell}} \left[g^{(j)}_{i, n}\right]^2 \left\{|g^{(j)}_{i, n}| \geq \varepsilon \mathbb{V}^{\frac{1}{2}}_n(r^{(j)}_n) \right\} d\mathbb{P}_{i,n} \to 0 \\ &\text{for every } \eps > 0, \end{aligned} \end{equation} and \begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \big|\mathbb{V}^{-1/2}_{n}\left(r_n^{(j)} \right) \Delta_n^{(j)} \big| \geq \eps \right) \to 0 \text{ for every } \eps > 0. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: $\hat{\theta}_n-\theta_n^*$ is a sum of independent centered summands plus a negligible remainder, with marginal Lindeberg conditions.

nodes.name: Condition X1
nodes.statement: Eventually $\rank(X_n) = p$, and for every $M\in\mathcal I$, \begin{equation*} \max_{i = 1, \hdots, n} X_{i,n}[M] \left( X_{n}[M]'X_{n}[M] \right)^{-1} X_{i,n}[M]' \to 0. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Full rank design eventually, and vanishing maximal leverage in every candidate submodel.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to homoskedastic data

nodes.name: Condition X2
nodes.statement: Let $C>0$ be fixed. Eventually, we have \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $\rank(X_n) = p$; \item $\max_{i = 1, \hdots, n} X_{i,n}[M] \left( X_{n}[M]'X_{n}[M] \right)^{-1} X_{i,n}[M]' \le C/n$, for every $M \in \mathcal{I}$; \item $\lmax(X_n'X_n)/\lmin(X_n'X_n) \le C$; \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Full rank, leverages of order $C/n$, and bounded eigenvalue ratio of $X_n'X_n$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data

nodes.name: Condition H
nodes.statement: The elements $h\in\mathcal H$ have the following properties: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item $h:\R\to(0,1)$ is a continuous cumulative distribution function; \item The functions $\phi_1(\gamma) := \log(h(\gamma))$ and $\phi_2(\gamma) := \log(1-h(\gamma))$ are strictly concave on $\R$; \item $h$ is twice continuously differentiable and $\phi_1$ and $\phi_2$ have strictly negative second derivatives on $\R$; \item The derivative $\dot{h}$ of $h$ is strictly positive on $\R$; \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Each response function is a smooth strictly increasing cdf with strictly log-concave $h$ and $1-h$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data

nodes.name: Condition 2
nodes.statement: For every $n \in \N$, every $j \in \{1, \hdots, k\}$ and every $i \in \{1, \hdots, n\}$ \begin{equation} \E_n(z^{(j)}_{i,n}) = 0 \quad \text{ and } \quad \mathbb{V}_n(r^{(j)}_n) = 1. \end{equation} Furthermore, for every $j \in \{1, \hdots, k\}$ we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \circ r^{(j)}_n \quad \Rightarrow \quad N(0,1), \end{equation} and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ \begin{equation} \max_{1 \leq i \leq n} \mathbb{P}_n\left(|z^{(j)}_{i,n}|\geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Standardised triangular array: centered summands, unit variance sums, marginal asymptotic normality and uniform negligibility.

nodes.name: Condition 3
nodes.statement: For every $n \in \N$, every $j \in \{1, \hdots, k\}$ and every $i \in \{1, \hdots, n\}$ we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{E}_n(z^{(j)}_{i,n}) = 0 \quad \text{ and } \quad 0 < \mathbb{V}_n(r^{(j)}_n) < \infty. \end{equation} Furthermore, setting $r^{(j)}_{n,*} = \frac{r^{(j)}_{n}}{\sqrt{\mathbb{V}_n(r^{(j)}_n)}}$ and $z^{(j)}_{i, n, *} = \frac{z^{(j)}_{i, n}}{\sqrt{\mathbb{V}_n(r^{(j)}_n)}}$, for every $j \in \{1, \hdots, k\}$ we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \circ r^{(j)}_{n,*} \Rightarrow N(0,1), \end{equation} and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ \begin{equation} \max_{1 \leq i \leq n} \mathbb{P}_n\left(|z^{(j)}_{i,n, *}|\geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0 \text{ as } n \to \infty. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Non-standardised version of Condition 2, phrased after dividing by $\mathbb{V}_n^{1/2}(r_n^{(j)})$.

nodes.name: The matrix $S_n$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} S_n(y) := \sum_{i = 1}^n g_{i,n}(y_i) g'_{i,n}(y_i), \end{equation}

nodes.name: Remark 2.1
nodes.statement: The careful reader will have noticed, that the functions $g_{i,n}:\R^{1\times\ell}\to\R^k$ in Condition~\ref{cond:sum} do not depend on all of the observation matrix $y\in\R^{n\times\ell}$, but only on its $i$-th row $y_i\in\R^{1\times\ell}$. This is crucial. In the sequel, however, it will be convenient to also consider $g_{i,n}$ as a function on the full sample space $\R^{n\times \ell}$. Thus, we sometimes identify $g_{i,n}$ with the composition $g_{i,n}\circ\pi_{i,n} : \R^{n\times \ell}\to \R^k$, where $\pi_{i,n}:\R^{n\times\ell}\to\R^{1\times\ell}$ is the coordinate projection $\pi_{i,n}(y) = y_i$.
nodes.statement_short: The $g_{i,n}$ depend only on row $i$; we nevertheless identify them with $g_{i,n}\circ\pi_{i,n}$ on the full sample space.

nodes.name: Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Under Condition \ref{cond:sum} \begin{equation*} d_w\left(\mathbb{P}_n \circ \left[\diag(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))^{\dagger/2} \left(\hat{\theta}_n - \theta_n^* \right)\right] , N\left(0, \corr(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))\right)\right) \to 0, \end{equation*} and, for every $\eps > 0$, it holds that \begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}_n \left(d_w\left(\mathbb{P}_n \circ \left[\diag(S_n)^{\dagger/2} \left(\hat{\theta}_n - \theta_n^* \right)\right] , N(0, \corr(S_n))\right) \geq \eps \right) \to 0. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Under Condition 1 the rescaled estimation error is well approximated by $N(0,\corr(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)))$, and also by $N(0,\corr(S_n))$ in probability.
assumptions: Under Condition \ref{cond:sum}
conclusions: \begin{equation*} d_w\left(\mathbb{P}_n \circ \left[\diag(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))^{\dagger/2} \left(\hat{\theta}_n - \theta_n^* \right)\right] , N\left(0, \corr(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))\right)\right) \to 0, \end{equation*}

and, for every $\eps > 0$, it holds that \begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}_n \left(d_w\left(\mathbb{P}_n \circ \left[\diag(S_n)^{\dagger/2} \left(\hat{\theta}_n - \theta_n^* \right)\right] , N(0, \corr(S_n))\right) \geq \eps \right) \to 0. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Remark 2.3
nodes.statement: Using, e.g., \cite{gnedenko} Theorem 3 in Paragraph 21, one obtains that Equation \eqref{eq:linde} in Condition \ref{cond:sum} can be \emph{equivalently} phrased as \begin{align*} \mathbb{P}_n\circ \left( \frac{r_n^{(j)}}{\mathbb{V}^{1/2}_n(r_n^{(j)})} \right) &\Rightarrow N(0, 1) \quad\text{and}\\[7pt] \max_{i = 1, \hdots, n} \mathbb{P}_n \left(|g_{i,n}^{(j)} | \geq \eps\mathbb{V}^{1/2}_n(r_n^{(j)}) \right) &\to 0\; \text{ for every } \eps > 0. \end{align*} In some applications it might be easier to check these two conditions directly (for every $j$), in particular in case one can use existing results in the literature on misspecified models without model selection as indicated above.
nodes.statement_short: The Lindeberg condition of Condition 1 is equivalent to marginal asymptotic normality plus uniform negligibility.

nodes.name: Offset $\rho(\mathbb{M})$
nodes.statement: Given $\mathbb{M} = \mathbb{M}_{j,n} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ we abbreviate \begin{equation*} \rho(\mathbb{M}) \quad := \quad \sum_{l = 1}^{j-1} m(\mathbb{M}_{l,n}), \end{equation*} where sums over an empty index set are to be interpreted as $0$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.4
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, suppose Condition \ref{cond:sum} holds, and let $\hat{S}_n: \R^{n \times \ell} \to \R^{k \times k}$ be a sequence of Borel-measurable functions so that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ \begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\corr(\hat{S}_n) - \corr\left(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)\right)\| + \| \diag(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))^{-1} \diag(\hat{S}_n) - I_k \| \geq \eps \right) \end{equation*} converges to $0$, or equivalently, that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\corr(\hat{S}_n) - \corr\left(S_n\right)\| + \| \diag(S_n)^{\dagger} \diag(\hat{S}_n) - I_k \| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0. \end{equation} Define for every $\mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ and every $j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M})$ the confidence interval \begin{equation*} \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}^{(j), \mathrm{est}} \quad = \quad \hat{\theta}^{(j)}_{\mathbb{M}, n} \pm \sqrt{[\hat{S}_n]_{\rho(\M) + j }} ~ K_{1-\alpha}\left(\corr(\hat{S}_n)\right). \end{equation*} Then, $ \mathbb{P}_n\left( \theta^{*(j)}_{\mathbb{M}, n} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}^{(j), \mathrm{est}} \text{ for all } \M\in\mathsf{M}_n \text{ and all } j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M}) \right) $ converges to $1-\alpha$ as $n\to\infty$. In particular, for every (measurable) model selection procedure $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$, we have \begin{equation} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{P}_n\left( \theta^{*(j)}_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n}^{(j), \mathrm{est}} \text{ for all } j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: If a consistent estimator $\hat{S}_n$ of $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$ exists, the POSI intervals attain exact asymptotic simultaneous coverage $1-\alpha$.
nodes.section: Confidence intervals based on consistent estimators of $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$
assumptions: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, suppose Condition \ref{cond:sum} holds, and let $\hat{S}_n: \R^{n \times \ell} \to \R^{k \times k}$ be a sequence of Borel-measurable functions so that for every $\varepsilon > 0$

\begin{equation*} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\corr(\hat{S}_n) - \corr\left(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)\right)\| + \| \diag(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))^{-1} \diag(\hat{S}_n) - I_k \| \geq \eps \right) \end{equation*} converges to $0$, or equivalently, that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\corr(\hat{S}_n) - \corr\left(S_n\right)\| + \| \diag(S_n)^{\dagger} \diag(\hat{S}_n) - I_k \| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0. \end{equation}
Define for every $\mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ and every $j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M})$ the confidence interval
conclusions: $ \mathbb{P}_n\left( \theta^{*(j)}_{\mathbb{M}, n} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}^{(j), \mathrm{est}} \text{ for all } \M\in\mathsf{M}_n \text{ and all } j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M}) \right) $ converges to $1-\alpha$ as $n\to\infty$. In particular, for every (measurable) model selection procedure $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$, we have

\begin{equation} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{P}_n\left( \theta^{*(j)}_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n}^{(j), \mathrm{est}} \text{ for all } j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 2.5
nodes.statement: Suppose Condition \ref{cond:sum} is satisfied, and let $\hat{g}_{i,n}: \R^{n \times \ell} \to \R^k$ be Borel measurable for $i = 1, \hdots, n$ and for every $n$. Suppose that for every $j = 1, \hdots, k$ and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ it holds that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n \left(g_{i,n}^{(j)} - \hat{g}_{i,n}^{(j)} \right)^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^n [g_{i,n}^{(j)}]^2} \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0, \end{equation} or equivalently that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n \left(g_{i,n}^{(j)} - \hat{g}_{i,n}^{(j)} \right)^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^n \mathbb{V}_n \left( g_{i,n}^{(j)}\right)} \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0. \end{equation} Then the convergence in \eqref{eq:consest} is satisfied for \begin{equation*} \hat{S}_n = \sum_{i = 1}^n \hat{g}_{i,n}\hat{g}'_{i,n}. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Predictors $\hat{g}_{i,n}$ whose squared error is negligible relative to $\sum_i [g^{(j)}_{i,n}]^2$ yield a consistent $\hat{S}_n=\sum_i\hat{g}_{i,n}\hat{g}'_{i,n}$.
nodes.section: Confidence intervals based on consistent estimators of $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$
assumptions: Suppose Condition \ref{cond:sum} is satisfied, and let $\hat{g}_{i,n}: \R^{n \times \ell} \to \R^k$ be Borel measurable for $i = 1, \hdots, n$ and for every $n$. Suppose that for every $j = 1, \hdots, k$ and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ it holds that

\begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n \left(g_{i,n}^{(j)} - \hat{g}_{i,n}^{(j)} \right)^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^n [g_{i,n}^{(j)}]^2} \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0, \end{equation} or equivalently that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n \left(g_{i,n}^{(j)} - \hat{g}_{i,n}^{(j)} \right)^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^n \mathbb{V}_n \left( g_{i,n}^{(j)}\right)} \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0. \end{equation}
conclusions: Then the convergence in \eqref{eq:consest} is satisfied for \begin{equation*} \hat{S}_n = \sum_{i = 1}^n \hat{g}_{i,n}\hat{g}'_{i,n}. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Theorem 2.6
nodes.statement_short: Estimators that asymptotically overestimate the variances and the POSI constant still give asymptotically valid post-model-selection intervals.
nodes.section: Confidence intervals based on estimators that consistently overestimate the diagonal entries of $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$
assumptions: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, and suppose Condition \ref{cond:sum} is satisfied. For every $n$ and every $j = 1, \hdots, k$ let $\hat{\nu}^2_{j,n} \geq 0$ be an estimator of $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n^{(j)})$, and let $\hat{K}_n \geq 0$ be an estimator of $K_{1-\alpha}(\corr(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)))$, so that the sequence

\begin{equation*} \kappa_n = \frac{K_{1-\alpha}(\corr(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)))}{\hat{K}_n} \max_{j = 1, \hdots, k} \sqrt{\frac{[\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)]_{j} }{ \hat{\nu}^2_{j,n} }}, \end{equation*} satisfies \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \kappa_n \geq 1+ \eps \right) \to 0 \text{ for every } \eps > 0, \end{equation}

For every $\mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ and every $j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M})$, define the confidence interval \begin{equation*} \mathrm{CI}_{1 - \alpha, \mathbb{M}}^{(j), \mathrm{oest}} \quad = \quad \hat{\theta}^{(j)}_{\mathbb{M}, n} \pm \sqrt{\hat{\nu}^2_{\rho(\M) + j, n}} ~ \hat{K}_n. \end{equation*}
conclusions: Then, for every (measurable) model selection procedure $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$, we have \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \theta_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n}^{*(j)} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1 - \alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n}^{(j), \mathrm{oest}} \text{ for all } j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation*}

In the important special case where $\hat{K}_n \geq K_{1-\alpha}(\corr(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)))$ holds eventually, the condition in Equation \eqref{eqn:asptup} is implied by the condition that for every $j = 1, \hdots, k$ it holds that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \sqrt{\frac{[S_n]_{j} }{ \hat{\nu}^2_{j,n} }} \geq 1+ \eps \right) \to 0 \text{ for every } \eps > 0, \end{equation} or equivalently, that for every $j = 1, \hdots, k$ it holds that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \sqrt{\frac{[\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)]_{j} }{ \hat{\nu}^2_{j,n} }} \geq 1+ \eps \right) \to 0 \text{ for every } \eps > 0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 2.7
nodes.statement: Suppose Condition \ref{cond:sum} is satisfied, and let $\tilde{g}_{i,n}: \R^{n \times \ell} \to \R^k$ and $\hat{g}_{i,n}: \R^{n \times \ell} \to \R^k$ be Borel measurable for $i = 1, \hdots, n$ and for every $n$. Suppose that for every $j = 1, \hdots, k$ and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ the condition \eqref{eq:negldiff}, or equivalently \eqref{eq:negldiff2}, is satisfied. Suppose further that there exist real numbers $a_{i,n}^{(j)}$ so that for $y\in\R^{n\times\ell}$ \begin{equation*} \tilde{g}^{(j)}_{i,n}(y) \quad = \quad \hat{g}^{(j)}_{i,n}(y) + a_{i,n}^{(j)} \end{equation*} holds for every $n \in \N$, $i \in \{1, \hdots, n\}$ and $j \in \{1, \hdots, k\}$. Then the statement in \eqref{eqn:special2} is satisfied for \begin{equation*} \hat{\nu}^2_{j,n} \quad = \quad \sum_{i = 1}^n \left[\tilde{g}^{(j)}_{i,n}\right]^2 \quad \text{ for } \quad j = 1, \hdots, k. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: If observable $\tilde{g}_{i,n}$ equal good predictors plus deterministic offsets, then $\hat{\nu}^2_{j,n}=\sum_i[\tilde{g}^{(j)}_{i,n}]^2$ consistently overestimates $[\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)]_j$.
nodes.section: Confidence intervals based on estimators that consistently overestimate the diagonal entries of $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$
assumptions: Suppose Condition \ref{cond:sum} is satisfied, and let $\tilde{g}_{i,n}: \R^{n \times \ell} \to \R^k$ and $\hat{g}_{i,n}: \R^{n \times \ell} \to \R^k$ be Borel measurable for $i = 1, \hdots, n$ and for every $n$. Suppose that for every $j = 1, \hdots, k$ and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ the condition \eqref{eq:negldiff}, or equivalently \eqref{eq:negldiff2}, is satisfied. Suppose further that there exist real numbers $a_{i,n}^{(j)}$ so that for $y\in\R^{n\times\ell}$

\begin{equation*} \tilde{g}^{(j)}_{i,n}(y) \quad = \quad \hat{g}^{(j)}_{i,n}(y) + a_{i,n}^{(j)} \end{equation*} holds for every $n \in \N$, $i \in \{1, \hdots, n\}$ and $j \in \{1, \hdots, k\}$. Then the statement in \eqref{eqn:special2} is satisfied for
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \hat{\nu}^2_{j,n} \quad = \quad \sum_{i = 1}^n \left[\tilde{g}^{(j)}_{i,n}\right]^2 \quad \text{ for } \quad j = 1, \hdots, k. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Remark 2.8
nodes.statement: Using the simple bound $(g_{i,n}^{(j)} - \tilde{g}_{i,n}^{(j)})^2 \le 2(g_{i,n}^{(j)} - \hat{g}_{i,n}^{(j)})^2 + 2 a_{i,n}^2$, it is easy to verify that if the non-stochastic additive components $a_{i,n}$ are negligible in the previously defined sense, then $\tilde{g}_{i,n}$ satisfies the assumptions of $\hat{g}_{i,n}$ appearing in Proposition \ref{prop:obtest}. As a consequence, the estimator \begin{equation*} \tilde{S}_n = \sum_{i = 1}^n \tilde{g}_{i,n}\tilde{g}'_{i,n} \end{equation*} satisfies \eqref{eq:consest}, and one can construct confidence intervals based on this estimator as discussed in Theorem \ref{thm:fbl}. Note that $\hat{\nu}^2_{j,n} = [\tilde{S}_n]_{j}$.
nodes.statement_short: If the deterministic offsets are negligible, $\tilde{S}_n$ is already a consistent estimator and Theorem 2.4 applies.
nodes.section: Confidence intervals based on estimators that consistently overestimate the diagonal entries of $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$

nodes.name: The quantity $B_{\alpha}(q,N)$
nodes.statement: Let us finally consider an upper bound on $K_{1-\alpha}(\Gamma)$ as required in the special case of Theorem \ref{thm:cons} above. The bound we shall discuss is based on the quantity $B_{\alpha}(q,N)$, for $q,N \in \mathbb{N}$, defined as the smallest $t >0$ so that \[ \mathbb{E}_G \left( \min\left(1, N \left[ 1 - F_{Beta,1/2,(q-1)/2} (t^2/G^2) \right] \right) \right) \leq \alpha, \] where $F_{Beta,1/2,(q-1)/2}$ is the cumulative distribution function of the \linebreak Beta($1/2$,$(q-1)/2$) distribution, and where $G^2$ follows a chi-squared distribution with $q$ degrees of freedom.
nodes.statement_short: $B_\alpha(q,N)$ is the smallest $t>0$ making a Beta/chi-square tail expectation at most $\alpha$.
nodes.section: Confidence intervals based on estimators that consistently overestimate the diagonal entries of $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$

nodes.name: Properties of $B_{\alpha}(q,N)$
nodes.statement: The quantity $B_{\alpha}(q,N)$ corresponds to the quantity $K_4$ of \cite{bachoc14valid} in the known variance case (for a discussion of numerical algorithms for obtaining $B_{\alpha}(q,N)$ in practice we confer the reader to that reference). We have \citep{bachoc14valid,Berk13} that $B_{\alpha}(q,N)$ is larger than all the $1-\alpha$ quantiles of random variables of the form $\max_{i=1,...,N} |v_i' \epsilon|$, where $v_1,...,v_N$ are column vectors of $\mathbb{R}^q$ with $||v_i|| \leq 1$ and where $\epsilon \sim N(0,I_q)$; furthermore, for fixed $\alpha$ and $N$ the function $q\mapsto B_{\alpha}(q, N)$ is monotonically increasing.
nodes.statement_short: $B_\alpha(q,N)$ dominates the $1-\alpha$ quantiles of $\max_i|v_i'\epsilon|$ over unit vectors, and increases in $q$.
nodes.section: Confidence intervals based on estimators that consistently overestimate the diagonal entries of $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$
nodes.origin_citation: Bachoc, Leeb & Pötscher 2014; Berk et al. 2013
conclusions: The quantity $B_{\alpha}(q,N)$ corresponds to the quantity $K_4$ of \cite{bachoc14valid} in the known variance case (for a discussion of numerical algorithms for obtaining $B_{\alpha}(q,N)$ in practice we confer the reader to that reference). We have \citep{bachoc14valid,Berk13} that $B_{\alpha}(q,N)$ is larger than all the $1-\alpha$ quantiles of random variables of the form $\max_{i=1,...,N} |v_i' \epsilon|$, where $v_1,...,v_N$ are column vectors of $\mathbb{R}^q$ with $||v_i|| \leq 1$ and where $\epsilon \sim N(0,I_q)$; furthermore, for fixed $\alpha$ and $N$ the function $q\mapsto B_{\alpha}(q, N)$ is monotonically increasing.

nodes.name: Asymptotic approximation of $B_{\alpha}(q,N)$
nodes.statement: Asymptotic approximations of $B_{\alpha}(q,N)$ for large $q$ and $N$ are provided in \cite{bachoc14valid}, \cite{Berk13} and \cite{zhang15spherical}. In particular, as $q,N \to \infty$, \[ B_{\alpha}(q,N)/\sqrt{q \left( 1-N ^{-2/\left( q-1\right) }\right) }\rightarrow 1, \] from Proposition 2.10 in \cite{bachoc14valid}, itself building on results from \cite{Berk13} and \cite{zhang15spherical}.
nodes.statement_short: $B_\alpha(q,N)/\sqrt{q(1-N^{-2/(q-1)})}\to1$ as $q,N\to\infty$.
nodes.section: Confidence intervals based on estimators that consistently overestimate the diagonal entries of $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$
nodes.origin_citation: Bachoc, Leeb & Pötscher 2014, Proposition 2.10; Berk et al. 2013; Zhang 2015
assumptions: as $q,N \to \infty$
conclusions: \[ B_{\alpha}(q,N)/\sqrt{q \left( 1-N ^{-2/\left( q-1\right) }\right) }\rightarrow 1, \]

nodes.name: Lemma 2.9
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and a $k \times k$ correlation matrix $\Gamma$ we have \[ K_{1-\alpha}(\Gamma) \leq B_{\alpha}(\rank(\Gamma),k). \]
nodes.statement_short: $K_{1-\alpha}(\Gamma)\le B_\alpha(\rank(\Gamma),k)$ for every correlation matrix $\Gamma$.
nodes.section: Confidence intervals based on estimators that consistently overestimate the diagonal entries of $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$
assumptions: For every $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and a $k \times k$ correlation matrix $\Gamma$
conclusions: \[ K_{1-\alpha}(\Gamma) \leq B_{\alpha}(\rank(\Gamma),k). \]

nodes.name: Feasible set $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}(\delta,\tau)$
nodes.statement: One important application of our general theory is the case where homoskedastic linear regression models are fit to data. The feasible sets for the true underlying distribution $\mathbb{P}_n$ we can allow for in this setup is denoted as $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}\left(\delta, \tau \right)$, where $\delta > 0$ and $\tau \ge 1$, and is defined as follows: the distribution $\P_n$ of the random $n$-vector $Y_n = (Y_{1,n}, \hdots, Y_{n,n})'$ is an element of $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}\left(\delta, \tau \right)$ if and only if the $n$ coordinates of $Y_n$ are independent, homoskedastic (i.e., the variances of the coordinates are equal to some $\V(Y_{i,n}) = \sigma_n^2 \in (0, \infty)$, for all $i=1,\dots, n$), and \begin{equation*} \max_{i = 1, \hdots, n} \mathbb{E}\left(|Y_{i,n} - \mathbb{E}(Y_{i,n})|^{2+\delta}\right)^{\frac{2}{2+\delta}} \leq \tau \sigma_n^2. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Independent homoskedastic coordinates whose $(2+\delta)$-moments are dominated by $\tau\sigma_n^2$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to homoskedastic data
nodes.genus: feasible set for the true underlying distribution $\mathbb{P}_n$
differentia: homoskedastic (i.e., the variances of the coordinates are equal to some $\V(Y_{i,n}) = \sigma_n^2 \in (0, \infty)$, for all $i=1,\dots, n$)

nodes.name: Homoskedastic linear candidate model $\mathbb{M}_{j,n}$
nodes.statement: We assume that we are given a nonempty set $\mathcal{I} = \{M_1, \hdots, M_d\}$ of nonempty subsets of $\{1, 2, \hdots, p\}$, that does not depend on $n$. Given $M \in \mathcal{I}$ we shall denote by $X_n[M]$ the matrix obtained from $X_n$ by striking all columns whose index is not an element of $M$. We then consider for each $j \in \{1, \hdots, d\}$ a linear, homoskedastic candidate model $\mathbb{M}_{j, n}$ with fixed design $X_n[M_j]$, i.e., the distribution of a random vector $z = (z_1, \hdots, z_n)'$ is an element of $\mathbb{M}_{j, n}$ if and only if there exists a $\beta \in \R^{|M_j|}$ so that the random (residual) vector $z - X_n[M_j]\beta$ has independent, homoskedastic coordinates with mean zero.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to homoskedastic data
nodes.genus: a linear, homoskedastic candidate model with fixed design $X_n[M_j]$
differentia: there exists a $\beta \in \R^{|M_j|}$ so that the random (residual) vector $z - X_n[M_j]\beta$ has independent, homoskedastic coordinates with mean zero

nodes.name: Remark 3.1
nodes.statement: Condition~\ref{cond:X} particularly holds if $\rank(X_n) = p$, eventually, and $\max_{i=1,\dots, n} X_{i,n}(X_n'X_n)^{-1}X_{i,n}' \to 0$. Moreover, it also holds in case $\|X_{i,n}\|$ is bounded and $\lambda_{\min}(\frac{1}{n} X_n'X_n)$ is bounded away from $0$, which is typically the case in sufficiently balanced factorial designs, but Condition~\ref{cond:X} is obviously much more general. For example, it also covers the important cases of polynomial regressors, trigonometric regressors, or mixed polynomial and trigonometric regressors (cf. the discussion in \cite{eicker67}, pp. 64). Finally, we point out that the condition \begin{equation*} \max_{i = 1, \hdots, n} X_{i,n}[M] \left( X_{n}[M]'X_{n}[M] \right)^{-1} X_{i,n}[M]' \to 0 \end{equation*} is classical, and is necessary for asymptotic normality of the ordinary-least-squares estimator in the fixed model $\M$ \citep[see][]{Huber73, Arnold80}.
nodes.statement_short: Condition X1 covers bounded rows with well-conditioned $X_n'X_n$, polynomial and trigonometric regressors, and is classical.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to homoskedastic data

nodes.name: Model-specific target $\beta_{\mathbb{M},n}^*$ (linear models)
nodes.statement: The model-specific target of inference is then (eventually) defined as follows: Given $\mathbb{M}\in \mathsf{M}_n$ with a corresponding index set $M$, we let \begin{equation} \beta_{\mathbb{M}, n}^* = \beta_{\mathbb{M}, n}^*(\mathbb{P}_n) = \left(X_n[M]'X_n[M]\right)^{-1} X_n[M]' \mu_n, \end{equation} i.e., $\beta_{\M,n}^*$ is the coefficient vector corresponding to the orthogonal projection of $\mu_n$ onto $\s(X_n[M])$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to homoskedastic data
nodes.genus: the coefficient vector corresponding to the orthogonal projection of $\mu_n$ onto $\s(X_n[M])$

nodes.name: Model-specific OLS estimator $\hat{\beta}_{\mathbb{M},n}$
nodes.statement: We shall now describe how asymptotically uniformly valid confidence sets can be constructed post-model-selection for the target defined in Equation \eqref{eqn:targethom} above: Given $\mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ with index set $M$, we estimate the corresponding target by the model-specific ordinary-least-squares estimator, i.e., by \begin{equation} \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb{M}, n}(y) = \left(X_n[M]'X_n[M]\right)^{-1} X_n[M]'y; \end{equation}
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to homoskedastic data

nodes.name: Variance estimator $\hat{\sigma}^2_{\mathbb{M},n}$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation*} \hat{\sigma}^2_{\mathbb{M}, n}(y) = \frac{1}{n- m(\mathbb{M})} \sum_{i = 1}^n (y_i - X_{i,n}[M] \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb{M}, n}(y) )^2, \end{equation*}
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to homoskedastic data

nodes.name: POSI confidence interval $\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha,\mathbb{M}}^{(j),\mathrm{lm}}$
nodes.statement: where $m(\mathbb{M})$ here coincides with $|M|$, the cardinality of $M$, and define for $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and $j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M})$ \begin{equation} \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}^{(j), \mathrm{lm}} = \hat{\beta}^{(j)}_{\mathbb{M}, n} \pm \sqrt{\hat{\sigma}^2_{\mathbb{M}, n} \left[\left( X_n[M]'X_n[M] \right)^{-1}\right]_j} K_{1-\alpha}(\corr(\Gamma_n)), \end{equation} where the block-matrix $\Gamma_n$ is defined via its $s,t$-th block of dimension $|M_s|\times|M_t|$ given by \begin{align*} &\E_n\left[ \left(\hat{\beta}_{\M_s,n} - \beta^*_{\M_s,n}\right) \left(\hat{\beta}_{\M_t,n} - \beta^*_{\M_t,n}\right)' \right] \\ &\quad= \sigma_n^2\left( X_n[M_s]' X_n[M_s] \right)^{-1} X_n[M_s]' X_n[M_t] \left( X_n[M_t]' X_n[M_t] \right)^{-1}, \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: The usual OLS interval with the normal quantile replaced by the POSI constant $K_{1-\alpha}(\corr(\Gamma_n))$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to homoskedastic data

nodes.name: Theorem 3.2
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, $\delta > 0$ and $\tau \ge 1$, suppose Condition~\ref{cond:X} holds, and let $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$ be a (measurable) model selection procedure, i.e., a measurable map from the sample space $\R^n$ to $\mathsf{M}_n$. Then \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \inf_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})} \left(\delta, \tau \right)} \mathbb{P}_n \left(\beta_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n}^{* (j)} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n}^{(j), \mathrm{lm}} \text{ for all } j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The POSI intervals cover all coordinates of the selected model's target simultaneously, uniformly over $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}(\delta,\tau)$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to homoskedastic data
assumptions: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, $\delta > 0$ and $\tau \ge 1$, suppose Condition~\ref{cond:X} holds, and let $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$ be a (measurable) model selection procedure, i.e., a measurable map from the sample space $\R^n$ to $\mathsf{M}_n$. Then
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \inf_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})} \left(\delta, \tau \right)} \mathbb{P}_n \left(\beta_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n}^{* (j)} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n}^{(j), \mathrm{lm}} \text{ for all } j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Individual-coefficient confidence interval $\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha,\mathbb{M}}$
nodes.statement: Finally, to define our confidence intervals in this case, let $\Xi_n$ denote the $d \times d$-dimensional matrix with $s,t$-th entry given by \begin{equation*} \sigma_n^2\left[ \left( X_n[M_s]' X_n[M_s] \right)^{-1} X_n[M_s]' X_n[M_t] \left( X_n[M_t]' X_n[M_t] \right)^{-1} \right]_{1}. \end{equation*} Given $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, define for every $\mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ with corresponding index set $M$ the confidence interval \begin{equation*} \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}} = \hat{\eta}_{\mathbb{M}, n} \pm \sqrt{\hat{\sigma}^2_{\mathbb{M}, n} \left[ (X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{-1} \right]_1} K_{1-\alpha}(\mathrm{corr}(\Xi_n)). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Same interval as $\mathrm{CI}^{(1),\mathrm{lm}}$ but with the smaller POSI constant $K_{1-\alpha}(\corr(\Xi_n))$.

nodes.name: Ordering of the POSI constants
nodes.statement: Note that, apart from the choice of the POSI constant, the confidence interval $\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}$ is identical to $\mathrm{CI}^{(1), \mathrm{lm}}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}$. While the latter interval is based on $K_{1-\alpha}(\mathrm{corr}(\Gamma_n))$, the POSI constant used here is $K_{1-\alpha}(\mathrm{corr}(\Xi_n))$. From the definition of $K_{1-\alpha}$, together with the relationship of $\Xi_n$ and $\Gamma_n$, it follows immediately that $$K_{1-\alpha}(\mathrm{corr}(\Xi_n)) \leq K_{1-\alpha}(\mathrm{corr}(\Gamma_n)),$$ with equality holding only if $\mathcal{I} = \{\{1\}\}$, i.e., no model selection. That is, the confidence intervals for individual parameters constructed here are smaller than the ones guaranteeing simultaneous coverage. The following can now be said about their asymptotic coverage properties.
nodes.statement_short: $K_{1-\alpha}(\corr(\Xi_n))\le K_{1-\alpha}(\corr(\Gamma_n))$, with equality only in the no-selection case.
conclusions: Note that, apart from the choice of the POSI constant, the confidence interval $\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}$ is identical to $\mathrm{CI}^{(1), \mathrm{lm}}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}$. While the latter interval is based on $K_{1-\alpha}(\mathrm{corr}(\Gamma_n))$, the POSI constant used here is $K_{1-\alpha}(\mathrm{corr}(\Xi_n))$. From the definition of $K_{1-\alpha}$, together with the relationship of $\Xi_n$ and $\Gamma_n$, it follows immediately that $$K_{1-\alpha}(\mathrm{corr}(\Xi_n)) \leq K_{1-\alpha}(\mathrm{corr}(\Gamma_n)),$$ with equality holding only if $\mathcal{I} = \{\{1\}\}$, i.e., no model selection. That is, the confidence intervals for individual parameters constructed here are smaller than the ones guaranteeing simultaneous coverage. The following can now be said about their asymptotic coverage properties.

nodes.name: Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, $\delta > 0$ and $\tau \ge 1$, suppose Condition~\ref{cond:X} holds, and let $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$ be a (measurable) model selection procedure. Suppose every element of $\mathcal{I}$ contains $1$. Then \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \inf_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})} \left(\delta, \tau \right)} \mathbb{P}_n \left(\eta^*_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n} \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The shorter individual-coefficient POSI interval is uniformly asymptotically valid for the first coefficient of the selected model.
assumptions: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, $\delta > 0$ and $\tau \ge 1$, suppose Condition~\ref{cond:X} holds, and let $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$ be a (measurable) model selection procedure. Suppose every element of $\mathcal{I}$ contains $1$. Then
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \inf_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})} \left(\delta, \tau \right)} \mathbb{P}_n \left(\eta^*_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n} \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Bias of the usual variance estimator under misspecification
nodes.statement: It is well known that the usual variance estimator $\hat{\sigma}_{\M,n}^2$ in model $\M\in\mathsf{M}_n$ with index set $M\in\mathcal I$ is consistent for the true error variance $\sigma_n^2$, if and only if, the model $\M$ is asymptotically first order correct. More specifically, the estimator $\hat{\sigma}_{\M,n}^2$ is upward biased when $\M$ is mean-misspecified and the bias is given by $\|(I_n - P_{X_n[M]})\mu_n/\sigma_n\|^2/(n-|M|)$, where $P_{\dots}$ denotes the projection matrix corresponding to the column span of the matrix indicated in the subscript and where $\mu_n = \E(Y_n)$.
nodes.statement_short: $\hat{\sigma}^2_{\M,n}$ is consistent iff the model is asymptotically first order correct; otherwise it is upward biased.
nodes.section: The POSI-intervals automatically adapt to misspecification
conclusions: the estimator $\hat{\sigma}_{\M,n}^2$ is upward biased when $\M$ is mean-misspecified and the bias is given by $\|(I_n - P_{X_n[M]})\mu_n/\sigma_n\|^2/(n-|M|)$

nodes.name: Proposition 3.4
nodes.statement: Fix $\delta>0$ and $\tau\ge 1$ and suppose that eventually $\rank(X_n)=p$. For any sequence $\P_n \in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}(\delta,\tau)$, the variance estimator $\hat{\sigma}_{\M,n}^2(y) = (n-|M|)^{-1}y'(I_n-P_{X_n[M]})y$ satisfies \begin{align*} \P_n\left( \left|\frac{\hat{\sigma}_{\M,n}^2}{\sigma_n^2} \left(1 + \frac{\|(I_n-P_{X_n[M]})\mu_n/\sigma_n\|^2}{n-|M|}\right)^{-1} - 1\right| > \eps \right) \;\to\;0, \end{align*} for every $\eps>0$ and for every $M\in\mathcal I$.
nodes.statement_short: $\hat{\sigma}^2_{\M,n}/\sigma_n^2$ is consistent for $1+\|(I_n-P_{X_n[M]})\mu_n/\sigma_n\|^2/(n-|M|)$, uniformly along sequences in $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}$.
nodes.section: The POSI-intervals automatically adapt to misspecification
assumptions: Fix $\delta>0$ and $\tau\ge 1$ and suppose that eventually $\rank(X_n)=p$. For any sequence $\P_n \in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}(\delta,\tau)$, the variance estimator $\hat{\sigma}_{\M,n}^2(y) = (n-|M|)^{-1}y'(I_n-P_{X_n[M]})y$ satisfies
conclusions: \begin{align*} \P_n\left( \left|\frac{\hat{\sigma}_{\M,n}^2}{\sigma_n^2} \left(1 + \frac{\|(I_n-P_{X_n[M]})\mu_n/\sigma_n\|^2}{n-|M|}\right)^{-1} - 1\right| > \eps \right) \;\to\;0, \end{align*} for every $\eps>0$ and for every $M\in\mathcal I$.

nodes.name: Consistency of the post-model-selection variance estimator
nodes.statement: In particular, since the index set $\mathcal I$ is finite, not depending on $n$, Proposition~\ref{prop:lmvarest} shows that the post-model-selection estimator $\hat{\sigma}_{\hat{\M}_n,n}^2$ is consistent for $\sigma_n^2$ (on a relative scale) along sequences $\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}(\delta,\tau)$ with the property that \begin{equation} \frac{\|(I_n-P_{X_n[\hat{M}_n]})\mu_n/\sigma_n\|^2}{n-|\hat{M}_n|} \;\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\; 0 \end{equation} in $\P_n$-probability, where $\hat{M}_n$ denotes the index set corresponding to $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$. Of course, in general, this condition can not be verified in practice. But it still tells us that if the model selection procedure $\hat{\M}_n$ finds an approximately first order correct model in the sense of \eqref{eq:CondCons}, then the POSI-intervals in \eqref{eq:POSICIlm} have the same asymptotic length as the infeasible intervals that use knowledge of $\sigma_n^2$.
nodes.statement_short: If the selected model is approximately first order correct, the POSI intervals have the same asymptotic length as the infeasible ones.
nodes.section: The POSI-intervals automatically adapt to misspecification
assumptions: since the index set $\mathcal I$ is finite, not depending on $n$
conclusions: In particular, since the index set $\mathcal I$ is finite, not depending on $n$, Proposition~\ref{prop:lmvarest} shows that the post-model-selection estimator $\hat{\sigma}_{\hat{\M}_n,n}^2$ is consistent for $\sigma_n^2$ (on a relative scale) along sequences $\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}(\delta,\tau)$ with the property that \begin{equation} \frac{\|(I_n-P_{X_n[\hat{M}_n]})\mu_n/\sigma_n\|^2}{n-|\hat{M}_n|} \;\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\; 0 \end{equation}

nodes.name: Existence of a uniformly consistent estimator of $\sigma_n^2$
nodes.statement: One can now raise the question whether it is at all possible to construct a uniformly (over $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}(\delta,\tau)$) consistent estimator for $\sigma_n^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Does a variance estimator consistent uniformly over $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}(\delta,\tau)$ exist?
nodes.section: The POSI-intervals automatically adapt to misspecification

nodes.name: Proposition 3.5
nodes.statement: Let $\delta > 0$ and $\tau > 1$. There does \emph{not} exist a sequence of measurable functions $(\hat{\sigma}^2_{n})_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $\hat{\sigma}^2_{n}: \mathbb{R}^n \to [0, \infty)$, so that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ \begin{equation} \sup_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}(\delta, \tau)} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \left| \frac{\hat{\sigma}^2_n}{\sigma^2_n} - 1 \right| > \varepsilon \right) \to 0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For $\tau>1$ no estimator of $\sigma_n^2$ is consistent uniformly over $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}(\delta,\tau)$.
nodes.section: The POSI-intervals automatically adapt to misspecification
assumptions: Let $\delta > 0$ and $\tau > 1$.
conclusions: Let $\delta > 0$ and $\tau > 1$. There does \emph{not} exist a sequence of measurable functions $(\hat{\sigma}^2_{n})_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with $\hat{\sigma}^2_{n}: \mathbb{R}^n \to [0, \infty)$, so that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ \begin{equation} \sup_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})}(\delta, \tau)} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \left| \frac{\hat{\sigma}^2_n}{\sigma^2_n} - 1 \right| > \varepsilon \right) \to 0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Feasible set $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{het})}(\delta,\tau)$
nodes.statement: The feasible sets for $\mathbb{P}_n$ we consider here again depend on two parameters $\delta > 0$ and $\tau \ge 1$ but, compared to the set $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{lm})} \left(\delta, \tau \right)$ defined above, we now drop the requirement of homoskedasticity: the distribution of a random $n$-vector $Y_n = (Y_{1,n}, \hdots, Y_{n,n})'$ is an element of $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{het})} \left(\delta, \tau \right)$ if and only if the $n$ coordinates of $Y_n$ are independent, the variance $\sigma_{i,n}^2 = \V(Y_{i,n}) \in(0,\infty)$ exists for every $i = 1, \hdots, n$, and \begin{equation*} \max_{i = 1, \hdots, n} \left[\mathbb{E}\left(|Y_{i,n} - \mathbb{E}(Y_{i,n})|\right)^{2+\delta}\right]^{\frac{2}{2+\delta}} \leq \tau \min_{i = 1, \hdots, n} \sigma_{i,n}^2. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Independent, possibly heteroskedastic coordinates whose $(2+\delta)$-moments are dominated by $\tau\min_i\sigma_{i,n}^2$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to heteroskedastic data
differentia: the variance $\sigma_{i,n}^2 = \V(Y_{i,n}) \in(0,\infty)$ exists for every $i = 1, \hdots, n$

nodes.name: Heteroskedastic linear candidate model $\mathbb{M}_{j,n}$
nodes.statement: We start with a set $\mathcal{I} = \{M_1, \hdots, M_d \}$ as in Subsection~\ref{sec:homlinmods}, and we then define for each $j \in \{1, \hdots, d\}$ the linear, heteroskedastic model $\mathbb{M}_{j, n}$ as follows: the distribution of a random vector $z = (z_1, \hdots, z_n)'$ is an element of $\mathbb{M}_{j, n}$ if and only if there exists a $\beta \in \R^{|M_j|}$ so that the random (residual) vector $z - X[M_j]\beta$ has independent coordinates with positive finite variances and mean zero.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to heteroskedastic data
differentia: there exists a $\beta \in \R^{|M_j|}$ so that the random (residual) vector $z - X[M_j]\beta$ has independent coordinates with positive finite variances and mean zero

nodes.name: Eicker-estimator $\tilde{S}_{\M,n}$
nodes.statement: Define for every $\mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ with corresponding index set $M$ the Eicker-estimator $\tilde{S}_{\M,n}$ as \begin{equation*} \left( X_n[M]'X_n[M] \right)^{-1} X_n[M]' \diag\left(\hat{u}^2_{1,\mathbb{M}}, \hdots, \hat{u}^2_{n,\mathbb{M}} \right) X_n[M] \left( X_n[M]'X_n[M] \right)^{-1}, \end{equation*} where, for $y\in\R^n$, we let $\hat{u}_{\mathbb{M}}(y) = (\hat{u}_{1, \mathbb{M}}(y), \hdots, \hat{u}_{n, \mathbb{M}}(y))' = y - X_n[M] \hat{\beta}_{\mathbb{M}, n}(y)$, and denote the $j-$th diagonal entry ($j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M})$) of $\tilde{S}_{\M,n}$ by $\hat{\sigma}^2_{j,\mathbb{M}, n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Sandwich variance estimator built from squared OLS residuals, following Eicker (1967).
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to heteroskedastic data

nodes.name: Confidence interval $\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha,\mathbb{M}}^{(j),\mathrm{hlm}}$
nodes.statement: Finally, given $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, we define for each $\mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ with corresponding index set $M$ and for every $j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M})$ the confidence sets \begin{equation*} \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}^{(j), \mathrm{hlm}} = \hat{\beta}^{(j)}_{\mathbb{M}, n} \pm \sqrt{\hat{\sigma}^2_{j,\mathbb{M}, n}} B_{\alpha}(\min(k, p),k), \end{equation*} with $k = \sum_{\M\in\mathsf{M}_n} m(\mathbb{M})$, and where $B_\alpha$ is defined at the end of Section~\ref{sec:overest}.
nodes.statement_short: Eicker-based interval with the POSI-constant upper bound $B_{\alpha}(\min(k,p),k)$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to heteroskedastic data

nodes.name: Theorem 3.6
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, $\delta > 0$ and $\tau \ge 1$, suppose Condition~\ref{cond:X} holds, and let $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$ be a (measurable) model selection procedure, i.e., a measurable map from the sample space $\R^n$ to $\mathsf{M}_n$. Then \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \inf_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{het})} \left(\delta, \tau \right) } \mathbb{P}_n \left(\beta_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n}^{* (j)} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n}^{(j), \mathrm{hlm}} \text{ for all } j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Eicker-type POSI intervals are uniformly asymptotically valid post-model-selection over $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{het})}(\delta,\tau)$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting fixed design linear models to heteroskedastic data
assumptions: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, $\delta > 0$ and $\tau \ge 1$, suppose Condition~\ref{cond:X} holds, and let $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$ be a (measurable) model selection procedure, i.e., a measurable map from the sample space $\R^n$ to $\mathsf{M}_n$. Then
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \inf_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{het})} \left(\delta, \tau \right) } \mathbb{P}_n \left(\beta_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n}^{* (j)} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n}^{(j), \mathrm{hlm}} \text{ for all } j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Feasible set $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)$
nodes.statement: The feasible sets $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)$ for $\P_n$ we consider here depend on a parameter $\tau \in (0,1/4)$ and are defined as follows: the distribution of a random vector $Y_n = (Y_{1,n}, \hdots, Y_{n,n})'$ is an element of $\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)$ if and only if the $n$ coordinates of $Y_n$ are independent, each coordinate $Y_{i,n}$ takes on either $0$ or $1$, and $\V(Y_{i,n})\ge \tau$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data
differentia: each coordinate $Y_{i,n}$ takes on either $0$ or $1$

nodes.name: Candidate binary regression model $\mathbb M_{(j_1,j_2),n}$
nodes.statement: Together with the collection $\mathcal I = \{M_1,\dots, M_{d_2}\}\subseteq 2^{\{1,\dots, p\}}\setminus\varnothing$ of candidate regressor subsets, we can define for every $j_1\in\{1,\dots, d_1\}$ and $j_2\in\{1,\dots, d_2\}$ a candidate binary regression model $\mathbb M_{(j_1,j_2),n}$ as follows: the distribution of a random vector $z = (z_1, \hdots, z_n)'$ is an element of $\mathbb M_{(j_1,j_2),n}$ if and only if the $n$ coordinates of $z$ are independent, each coordinate $z_i$ takes on either $0$ or $1$, and there exists a $\beta \in \R^{|M_{j_2}|}$ so that the mean of $z_i$ equals $h_{j_1}(X_{i,n}[M_{j_2}]\beta)$ for $i = 1, \hdots, n$.
nodes.statement_short: A candidate model is a pair (response function, regressor subset) with means $h_{j_1}(X_{i,n}[M_{j_2}]\beta)$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data
differentia: the $n$ coordinates of $z$ are independent, each coordinate $z_i$ takes on either $0$ or $1$
there exists a $\beta \in \R^{|M_{j_2}|}$ so that the mean of $z_i$ equals $h_{j_1}(X_{i,n}[M_{j_2}]\beta)$ for $i = 1, \hdots, n$

nodes.name: Remark 3.7
nodes.statement: Condition~\ref{cond:X2} is a strengthened version of Condition~\ref{cond:X}. It is still satisfied if $\|X_{i,n}\|$ is bounded and $\lmin(\frac{1}{n}X_n'X_n)$ is bounded away from $0$, as is typically the case in factorial designs. Note, however, that Condition~\ref{cond:X2} is invariant under scaling of $X_n$, so that, in particular, it does not require that $\lmin(X_n'X_n)\to\infty$, a condition commonly used to prove consistency of the MLE. Furthermore, Condition~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:Huber} is implied by $$ X2(ii')\quad\max_{i=1,\dots, n} X_{i,n}(X_n'X_n)^{-1}X_{i,n}' \le C/n. $$
nodes.statement_short: Condition X2 strengthens X1, is scale invariant, and is implied by a global leverage bound.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data

nodes.name: Remark 3.8
nodes.statement: The Conditions~\ref{cond:H}\eqref{cH:cdf} and \ref{cond:H}\eqref{cH:Hdot} are rather natural and essential for parameter identification. Condition~\ref{cond:H}\eqref{cH:C2} is also classical and used to ensure continuity of the Hessian of the log-likelihood \citep[cf.][]{Fahrmeir85, Fahrmeir90}. Finally, Condition~\ref{cond:H}\eqref{cH:concave}, which is implied by Condition~\ref{cond:H}\eqref{cH:C2}, ensures strict concavity of the log-likelihood, which, in turn, guarantees uniqueness of pseudo parameters and the MLE (see Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudo} and Lemma~\ref{lemma:unifCons} below). It is easy to see that Condition~\ref{cond:H} is satisfied, e.g., for response functions corresponding to the classical logit, probit, log-log and complementary log-log link functions discussed in \citet[][p.108]{McCullagh89}.
nodes.statement_short: The parts of Condition H are natural, ensure identification and strict log-concavity, and hold for logit, probit and (complementary) log-log.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data

nodes.name: Quasi-log-likelihood $\ell_{\M,n}$ and Hessian $H_{\M,n}$
nodes.statement: Estimating the parameter $\beta\in\R^{|M|}$ of a candidate model $\M\in\mathsf{M}_n$ is usually done by numerically maximizing the likelihood. The (quasi-)log-likelihood function for model $\M \triangleq (h,M)$ can be expressed as \begin{equation*} \ell_{\M,n}(y,\beta) \;=\; \sum_{i=1}^n \left[ y_i \phi_1(X_{i,n}[M]\beta) + (1-y_i)\phi_2(X_{i,n}[M]\beta)\right], \end{equation*} where $\phi_1(\gamma) = \log h(\gamma)$ and $\phi_2(\gamma) = \log (1-h(\gamma))$, and $y = (y_1,\dots, y_n)'\in\{0,1\}^n$, $\beta\in\R^{|M|}$. Whenever Condition~\ref{cond:H}\eqref{cH:C2} holds, we denote the matrix of negative second derivatives of $\ell_{\M,n}$ by $$ H_{\M,n}(y,\beta) \;=\; -\frac{\partial^2\ell_{\M,n}(y,\beta)}{\partial \beta \partial \beta'} \;=\; X_n[M]'D_{\M,n}(y,\beta)X_n[M], $$ where $D_{\M,n}(y,\beta)$ is a diagonal matrix with $i$-th diagonal entry equal to $$-y_i \ddot{\phi}_1(X_{i,n}[M]\beta) - (1-y_i)\ddot{\phi}_2(X_{i,n}[M]\beta).$$
nodes.statement_short: Log-likelihood $\sum_i[y_i\phi_1+(1-y_i)\phi_2]$ with $\phi_1=\log h$, $\phi_2=\log(1-h)$, and $H_{\M,n}=X'DX$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data

nodes.name: Positive definiteness of $H_{\M,n}$
nodes.statement: Note that under Conditions~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:rank} and \ref{cond:H}\eqref{cH:C2}, $H_{\M,n}(y,\beta)$ is positive definite.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data
conclusions: Note that under Conditions~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:rank} and \ref{cond:H}\eqref{cH:C2}, $H_{\M,n}(y,\beta)$ is positive definite.

nodes.name: Kullback-Leibler target $\beta_{\M,n}^*$ (binary regression)
nodes.statement: As our target of inference we take the model dependent vector $\beta_{\M,n}^* \in\R^{|M|}$ that maximizes the expected log-likelihood $\beta\mapsto \E_n[\ell_{\M,n}(\cdot,\beta)]$ under the true data generating distribution $\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)$. If $\beta_{\M,n}^*$ exists, then it is easy to see that it also minimizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the true data generating distribution $\P_n$ and the class of distributions specified by the working model $\M\in\mathsf{M}_n$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data
nodes.genus: the model dependent vector that maximizes the expected log-likelihood
differentia: $\beta\mapsto \E_n[\ell_{\M,n}(\cdot,\beta)]$ under the true data generating distribution $\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)$
it also minimizes the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the true data generating distribution $\P_n$ and the class of distributions specified by the working model $\M\in\mathsf{M}_n$

nodes.name: Lemma 3.9
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\rank(X_n)=p$ and \ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:cdf},\ref{cH:concave}) hold. Then, for every $\M\in\mathsf{M}_n$ and for every $\P_n\in\bigcup_{\delta>0}\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\delta)$, there exists a unique vector $\beta_{\M,n}^* = \beta_{\M,n}^*(\P_n)\in\R^{m(\M)}$, such that \begin{equation*} \int_{\R^n} \ell_{\M,n}(y,\beta_{\M,n}^*(\P_n)) \,d\P_n(y) \;=\; \sup_{\beta\in\R^{m(\M)}} \int_{\R^n} \ell_{\M,n}(y,\beta) \,d\P_n(y). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The Kullback-Leibler pseudo parameter of a binary regression candidate model exists and is unique.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data
assumptions: Suppose that $\rank(X_n)=p$ and \ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:cdf},\ref{cH:concave}) hold.
conclusions: Suppose that $\rank(X_n)=p$ and \ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:cdf},\ref{cH:concave}) hold. Then, for every $\M\in\mathsf{M}_n$ and for every $\P_n\in\bigcup_{\delta>0}\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\delta)$, there exists a unique vector $\beta_{\M,n}^* = \beta_{\M,n}^*(\P_n)\in\R^{m(\M)}$, such that \begin{equation*} \int_{\R^n} \ell_{\M,n}(y,\beta_{\M,n}^*(\P_n)) \,d\P_n(y) \;=\; \sup_{\beta\in\R^{m(\M)}} \int_{\R^n} \ell_{\M,n}(y,\beta) \,d\P_n(y). \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Non-existence of the MLE on some samples
nodes.statement: Furthermore, it is well known that for some points in the sample space $\{0,1\}^n$ the MLE in the binary regression model does not exist \citep[see, e.g.,][]{Wedderburn76}. But those samples have vanishing asymptotic probability.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data
conclusions: for some points in the sample space $\{0,1\}^n$ the MLE in the binary regression model does not exist

nodes.name: Lemma 3.10
nodes.statement: Suppose that Conditions~\ref{cond:X2}(\ref{cX2:rank},\ref{cX2:Huber}) and \ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:cdf},\ref{cH:concave},\ref{cH:C2}) hold and fix $\tau\in(0,1/4)$. Then, for every $n\in\N$, every $\M\in\mathsf{M}_n$ and every $\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)$, there exists a function $\hat{\beta}_{\M,n}:\{0,1\}^n\to\R^{m(\M)}$ (depending only on $n$ and $\M$) and a set $E_{\M,\P_n,n}\subseteq \{0,1\}^n$, such that \begin{align*} \ell_{\M,n}\left(y, \hat{\beta}_{\M,n}(y) + \beta\right) \;<\; \ell_{\M,n}\left(y, \hat{\beta}_{\M,n}(y)\right) \quad \forall y\in\ E_{\M,\P_n,n},\;\forall \beta\neq 0 \end{align*} and $$\inf_{\M\in\mathsf{M}_n}\inf_{\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)} \P_n(E_{\M,\P_n,n}) \;\xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{} \; 1.$$ Moreover, for the pseudo parameter $\beta_{\M,n}^*\in\R^{m(\M)}$ of Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudo}, we have $$ \limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\substack{\M\in\mathsf{M}_n\\\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)}} \P_n\left( \left\| (X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{1/2}(\hat{\beta}_{\M,n} - \beta^*_{\M,n}(\P_n))\right\| > \delta\right)\; \to\; 0, $$ as $\delta\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: The (quasi-)MLE exists with probability tending to one, uniformly in the model and the data generating distribution, and is uniformly consistent for the pseudo parameter.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data
assumptions: Suppose that Conditions~\ref{cond:X2}(\ref{cX2:rank},\ref{cX2:Huber}) and \ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:cdf},\ref{cH:concave},\ref{cH:C2}) hold and fix $\tau\in(0,1/4)$.
conclusions: Suppose that Conditions~\ref{cond:X2}(\ref{cX2:rank},\ref{cX2:Huber}) and \ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:cdf},\ref{cH:concave},\ref{cH:C2}) hold and fix $\tau\in(0,1/4)$. Then, for every $n\in\N$, every $\M\in\mathsf{M}_n$ and every $\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)$, there exists a function $\hat{\beta}_{\M,n}:\{0,1\}^n\to\R^{m(\M)}$ (depending only on $n$ and $\M$) and a set $E_{\M,\P_n,n}\subseteq \{0,1\}^n$, such that \begin{align*} \ell_{\M,n}\left(y, \hat{\beta}_{\M,n}(y) + \beta\right) \;<\; \ell_{\M,n}\left(y, \hat{\beta}_{\M,n}(y)\right) \quad \forall y\in\ E_{\M,\P_n,n},\;\forall \beta\neq 0 \end{align*} and $$\inf_{\M\in\mathsf{M}_n}\inf_{\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)} \P_n(E_{\M,\P_n,n}) \;\xrightarrow[n\to \infty]{} \; 1.$$

Moreover, for the pseudo parameter $\beta_{\M,n}^*\in\R^{m(\M)}$ of Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudo}, we have $$ \limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\substack{\M\in\mathsf{M}_n\\\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)}} \P_n\left( \left\| (X_n[M]'X_n[M])^{1/2}(\hat{\beta}_{\M,n} - \beta^*_{\M,n}(\P_n))\right\| > \delta\right)\; \to\; 0, $$ as $\delta\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Sandwich estimator $\tilde{S}_{\M,n}$ (binary regression)
nodes.statement: For $\M\in\mathsf{M}_n$, $\M \triangleq (h,M)$, define \begin{align} \tilde{S}_{\M,n} = \hat{H}_{\M,n}^{-1}X_n[M]' \diag\left(\hat{u}^2_{1,\mathbb{M}}, \hdots, \hat{u}^2_{n,\mathbb{M}} \right) X_n[M] \hat{H}_{\M,n}^{-1}, \end{align} where $\hat{H}_{\M,n}(y) = H_{\M,n}(y,\hat{\beta}_{\M,n}(y))$, $$ \hat{u}_{i,\mathbb{M}}(y) = \frac{\dot{h}(\hat{\gamma}_{i,n,M}(y))}{h(\hat{\gamma}_{i,n,M}(y))(1-h(\hat{\gamma}_{i,n,M}(y)))}\left(y_i - h(\hat{\gamma}_{i,n,M}(y)) \right) $$ and $\hat{\gamma}_{i,n,M}(y) = X_{i,n}[M]\hat{\beta}_{\M,n}(y)$, and denote the $j-$th diagonal entry ($j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M})$) of $\tilde{S}_{\M,n}$ by \begin{equation} \hat{\sigma}^2_{j,\mathbb{M}, n}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Fahrmeir-Kaufmann style sandwich estimator $\hat{H}^{-1}X'\diag(\hat u^2)X\hat{H}^{-1}$ built from working residuals.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data

nodes.name: Confidence interval $\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha,\mathbb{M}}^{(j),\mathrm{bin}}$
nodes.statement: Finally, given $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, we define for each $\mathbb{M} \in \mathsf{M}_n$ and for every $j = 1, \hdots, m(\mathbb{M})$ the confidence sets \begin{equation*} \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \mathbb{M}}^{(j), \mathrm{bin}} = \hat{\beta}^{(j)}_{\mathbb{M}, n} \pm \sqrt{\hat{\sigma}^2_{j,\mathbb{M}, n}} B_{\alpha}(\min(k, n),k), \end{equation*} with $k = \sum_{\M\in\mathsf{M}_n} m(\mathbb{M})$, and where $B_\alpha$ is as defined at the end of Section~\ref{sec:overest}.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data

nodes.name: Theorem 3.11
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and $\tau \in(0,1/4)$, suppose Conditions~\ref{cond:X2} and \ref{cond:H} hold, and let $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$ be a model selection procedure, i.e., a map from the sample space $\{0,1\}^n$ to $\mathsf{M}_n$. Then \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \inf_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})} \left(\tau \right) } \mathbb{P}_n \left(\beta_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n}^{* (j)} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n}^{(j), \mathrm{bin}} \;\forall j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Sandwich-based POSI intervals for binary regression are uniformly asymptotically valid for any data-driven choice of regressors and link.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data
assumptions: Let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and $\tau \in(0,1/4)$, suppose Conditions~\ref{cond:X2} and \ref{cond:H} hold, and let $\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n$ be a model selection procedure, i.e., a map from the sample space $\{0,1\}^n$ to $\mathsf{M}_n$. Then
conclusions: \begin{equation*} \liminf_{n \to \infty} \inf_{\mathbb{P}_n \in \mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})} \left(\tau \right) } \mathbb{P}_n \left(\beta_{\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n, n}^{* (j)} \in \mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha, \hat{\mathbb{M}}_n}^{(j), \mathrm{bin}} \;\forall j = 1, \hdots, m(\hat{\mathbb{M}}_n) \right) \geq 1-\alpha. \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Remark 3.12
nodes.statement: It is important to note that if one decides a priori to use only the canonical link function, which, in the present case of binary regression, corresponds to the logistic response function $h^{(c)}(\gamma) := e^\gamma/(1+e^\gamma)$, then Theorem~\ref{thm:binary} holds with the POSI-constant $B_\alpha(\min(k,n),k)$ decreased to $B_\alpha(\min(k,p),k)$. See Corollary~\ref{corr:binaryCanoncial} in Section~\ref{sec:binaryCanonical} of the supplement.
nodes.statement_short: With the canonical logistic response function alone the POSI constant sharpens to $B_\alpha(\min(k,p),k)$.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data

nodes.name: Remark 3.13
nodes.statement: We point out that similar principles used to derive Theorem~\ref{thm:binary} can also be employed to treat other quasi-maximum likelihood or general M-, and Z-estimation problems \citep[see, e.g.,][for a more general treatment of generalized linear models]{Fahrmeir90}. The general theory of M- and Z-estimation as presented, e.g., in \citet[][Sections~3.2 and 3.3]{Vaart96}, usually also leads to expansions of the form required in Conditon~\ref{cond:sum} \citep[cf.][Theorem~3.2.16 and Theorem~3.3.1]{Vaart96}. These results are stated in a pointwise fashion but can be made uniform over large classes of data generating processes by using ideas from Section~2.8 of the same reference. However, in more specific examples, such as the present binary regression setting, conditions can be directly imposed on the design and the link functions and can be optimized for this setup.
nodes.statement_short: The same principles extend to general M- and Z-estimation, where expansions as in Condition 1 are standard.
nodes.section: Inference post-model-selection when fitting binary regression models to binary data

nodes.name: Open questions currently under investigation
nodes.statement: Open questions that go beyond the scope of this article, but are currently under investigation, include the extension of the approach discussed here to dependent data; the applicability and performance of bootstrap procedures; and the development of procedures in the spirit of \cite{Berk13} in the challenging situation when the number of models fitted can grow with sample size. In ongoing work we apply our methods to real data and investigate if they can prevent spurious findings while detecting true reproducible effects.
nodes.statement_short: Extensions to dependent data, bootstrap procedures, and a growing number of candidate models remain open.

nodes.name: Lemma B.1
nodes.statement: Suppose Condition~\ref{cond:zmom} holds. Then \begin{equation} d_w \big( \mathbb{P}_n \circ r_n, N(0, \mathbb{V}_n(r_n)) \big) \to 0. \end{equation} Furthermore, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ it holds that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left(\big \|S_n -\mathbb{V}_n(r_n) \big \| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0, \end{equation} and hence that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( d_w \big( \mathbb{P}_n \circ r_n, N(0, S_n) \big) \geq \varepsilon\right) \to 0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Under Condition 2 the row sums are asymptotically $N(0,\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))$ and the empirical second-moment matrix $S_n$ is consistent for $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$.
assumptions: Suppose Condition~\ref{cond:zmom} holds.
conclusions: \begin{equation} d_w \big( \mathbb{P}_n \circ r_n, N(0, \mathbb{V}_n(r_n)) \big) \to 0. \end{equation}
\begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left(\big \|S_n -\mathbb{V}_n(r_n) \big \| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0, \end{equation}
\begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( d_w \big( \mathbb{P}_n \circ r_n, N(0, S_n) \big) \geq \varepsilon\right) \to 0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma B.2
nodes.statement: Suppose Condition~\ref{cond:zmomstd} holds. Then, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\diag(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))^{-1} \diag(S_n) - I_k\| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0 \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\corr \left( S_n \right) - \corr \left( \mathbb{V}_n(r_n) \right)\| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0. \end{equation} Furthermore, for every $\eps > 0$, $\hat{r}_{n,*} = \diag(S_n)^{\dagger/2} ~ r_n$ satisfies \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left(d_w\left(\mathbb{P}_n \circ \hat{r}_{n,*} , N(0, \corr(S_n))\right) \geq \eps \right) \rightarrow 0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Non-standardised version of Lemma B.1: diagonal and correlation consistency of $S_n$, plus a conditional CLT for $\diag(S_n)^{\dagger/2}r_n$.
assumptions: Suppose Condition~\ref{cond:zmomstd} holds.
conclusions: \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\diag(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))^{-1} \diag(S_n) - I_k\| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0 \end{equation}
\begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\corr \left( S_n \right) - \corr \left( \mathbb{V}_n(r_n) \right)\| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0. \end{equation}

Furthermore, for every $\eps > 0$, $\hat{r}_{n,*} = \diag(S_n)^{\dagger/2} ~ r_n$ satisfies \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left(d_w\left(\mathbb{P}_n \circ \hat{r}_{n,*} , N(0, \corr(S_n))\right) \geq \eps \right) \rightarrow 0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma B.3
nodes.statement: For every $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ the map $\Gamma \mapsto K_{1-\alpha}(\Gamma)$ is continuous on the subset of $k \times k$-dimensional covariance matrices of $\R^{k \times k}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Gamma\mapsto K_{1-\alpha}(\Gamma)$ is continuous on the set of $k\times k$ covariance matrices.
assumptions: For every $\alpha \in (0, 1)$
conclusions: For every $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ the map $\Gamma \mapsto K_{1-\alpha}(\Gamma)$ is continuous on the subset of $k \times k$-dimensional covariance matrices of $\R^{k \times k}$.

nodes.name: Lemma B.4
nodes.statement: For $n \in \N$, for every $i = 1, \hdots, n$, and for $j = 1, 2$, let $a_{i,n}(j)$ and $b_{i,n}(j)$ be random variables on a probability space $(\Omega_n, \mathcal{A}_n, \mathbb{P}_n)$. Furthermore, let $a_{i,n}=a_{i,n}(1)$ and $b_{i,n}=b_{i,n}(1)$. \begin{enumerate} \item If $\mathbb{P}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n} = 0) \to 0$ holds, and if $\frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n (a_{i,n} - b_{i,n})^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n} } = o_{\mathbb{P}_n}(1)$, then \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \bigg| \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n b^2_{i,n} }{\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n}} - 1 \bigg| \geq \eps \right) \to 0 \quad \text{ for every } \eps > 0. \end{equation} \item If $\mathbb{P}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n}(j) = 0) \to 0$ and $\frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n (a_{i,n}(j) - b_{i,n}(j))^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n}(j) } = o_{\mathbb{P}_n}(1)$ holds for $j = 1, 2$, then for every $\eps > 0$ \begin{align} &\mathbb{P}_n \bigg( \bigg | \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n}(1) a_{i,n}(2)}{\sqrt{\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n}^2(1) } \sqrt{ \sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n}(2)}} \\[7pt] & \hspace{3cm} - \quad \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n b_{i,n}(1) b_{i,n}(2)}{\sqrt{\sum_{i = 1}^n b_{i,n}^2(1)} \sqrt{\sum_{i = 1}^n b^2_{i,n}(2)}} \bigg | \geq \eps \bigg) \to 0. \end{align} \item Suppose that $\mathbb{V}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n}) > 0$ holds eventually. Assume that for every $n$ the random variables $a_{i,n}$ for $i = 1, \hdots, n$ have mean $0$ and are uncorrelated, and that it holds that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n\left(\bigg|\frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n}}{\mathbb{V}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n})} - 1\bigg| > \eps\right) \to 0 \text{ for every } \eps > 0, \end{equation} that \begin{equation} \frac{\max_{i = 1, \hdots, n} \mathbb{V}_n(a_{i,n})} {\mathbb{V}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n})} \to 0, \end{equation} and that $\frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n (a_{i,n} - b_{i,n})^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n} } = o_{\mathbb{P}_n}(1)$. Then for every array of real numbers $c_{i,n}$ we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n (b_{i,n} + c_{i,n})^2}{\mathbb{V}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n})} \leq 1 - \eps \right) \to 0 \quad \text{ for every } \eps > 0. \end{equation} \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Three ratio-stability results for triangular arrays whose approximation error is negligible relative to $\sum_i a_{i,n}^2$.
assumptions: For $n \in \N$, for every $i = 1, \hdots, n$, and for $j = 1, 2$, let $a_{i,n}(j)$ and $b_{i,n}(j)$ be random variables on a probability space $(\Omega_n, \mathcal{A}_n, \mathbb{P}_n)$. Furthermore, let $a_{i,n}=a_{i,n}(1)$ and $b_{i,n}=b_{i,n}(1)$.
conclusions: \item If $\mathbb{P}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n} = 0) \to 0$ holds, and if $\frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n (a_{i,n} - b_{i,n})^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n} } = o_{\mathbb{P}_n}(1)$, then \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \bigg| \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n b^2_{i,n} }{\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n}} - 1 \bigg| \geq \eps \right) \to 0 \quad \text{ for every } \eps > 0. \end{equation}

\item If $\mathbb{P}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n}(j) = 0) \to 0$ and $\frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n (a_{i,n}(j) - b_{i,n}(j))^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n}(j) } = o_{\mathbb{P}_n}(1)$ holds for $j = 1, 2$, then for every $\eps > 0$ \begin{align} &\mathbb{P}_n \bigg( \bigg | \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n}(1) a_{i,n}(2)}{\sqrt{\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n}^2(1) } \sqrt{ \sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n}(2)}} \\[7pt] & \hspace{3cm} - \quad \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n b_{i,n}(1) b_{i,n}(2)}{\sqrt{\sum_{i = 1}^n b_{i,n}^2(1)} \sqrt{\sum_{i = 1}^n b^2_{i,n}(2)}} \bigg | \geq \eps \bigg) \to 0. \end{align}

\item Suppose that $\mathbb{V}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n}) > 0$ holds eventually. Assume that for every $n$ the random variables $a_{i,n}$ for $i = 1, \hdots, n$ have mean $0$ and are uncorrelated, and that it holds that \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n\left(\bigg|\frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n}}{\mathbb{V}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n})} - 1\bigg| > \eps\right) \to 0 \text{ for every } \eps > 0, \end{equation} that \begin{equation} \frac{\max_{i = 1, \hdots, n} \mathbb{V}_n(a_{i,n})} {\mathbb{V}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n})} \to 0, \end{equation} and that $\frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n (a_{i,n} - b_{i,n})^2}{\sum_{i = 1}^n a^2_{i,n} } = o_{\mathbb{P}_n}(1)$. Then for every array of real numbers $c_{i,n}$ we have \begin{equation} \mathbb{P}_n \left( \frac{\sum_{i = 1}^n (b_{i,n} + c_{i,n})^2}{\mathbb{V}_n(\sum_{i = 1}^n a_{i,n})} \leq 1 - \eps \right) \to 0 \quad \text{ for every } \eps > 0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma C.1
nodes.statement: Under Condition \ref{cond:sum}, for $\eps > 0$ we have \begin{align*} &\mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\diag(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))^{-1} \diag(S_n) - I_k\| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0, \\[7pt] &\mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\corr \left( S_n \right) - \corr \left( \mathbb{V}_n(r_n) \right)\| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0 \quad\text{and}\\[7pt] &\mathbb{P}_n \left(d_w\left(\mathbb{P}_n \circ \left[\diag(S_n)^{\dagger/2} \left(\hat{\theta}_n - \theta_n^* \right)\right] , N(0, \corr(S_n))\right) \geq \eps \right) \to 0. \end{align*} The last statement remains valid upon replacing $S_n$ by $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$ and then reduces to $d_w\left(\mathbb{P}_n \circ \left[\diag(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))^{\dagger/2} \left(\hat{\theta}_n - \theta_n^* \right)\right] , N(0, \corr(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)))\right) \to 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Detailed version of Lemma 2.2: adds the diagonal- and correlation-consistency statements for $S_n$.
assumptions: Under Condition \ref{cond:sum}, for $\eps > 0$
conclusions: \begin{align*} &\mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\diag(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))^{-1} \diag(S_n) - I_k\| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0, \\[7pt] &\mathbb{P}_n \left( \|\corr \left( S_n \right) - \corr \left( \mathbb{V}_n(r_n) \right)\| \geq \varepsilon \right) \to 0 \quad\text{and}\\[7pt] &\mathbb{P}_n \left(d_w\left(\mathbb{P}_n \circ \left[\diag(S_n)^{\dagger/2} \left(\hat{\theta}_n - \theta_n^* \right)\right] , N(0, \corr(S_n))\right) \geq \eps \right) \to 0. \end{align*}

The last statement remains valid upon replacing $S_n$ by $\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)$ and then reduces to $d_w\left(\mathbb{P}_n \circ \left[\diag(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n))^{\dagger/2} \left(\hat{\theta}_n - \theta_n^* \right)\right] , N(0, \corr(\mathbb{V}_n(r_n)))\right) \to 0$.

nodes.name: Lemma D.1
nodes.statement: Suppose that Conditions~\ref{cond:X2}(\ref{cX2:rank},\ref{cX2:Huber}) and \ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:cdf},\ref{cH:concave}) hold and fix $\tau\in(0,1/4)$. There exists a finite positive constant $K^*(\tau, C)$, depending only on $\tau$ and the constant $C$ from Condition~\ref{cond:X2}\eqref{cX2:Huber}, such that eventually $$ \sup_{\substack{\M\in\mathsf{M}_n\\\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)}} \max_{i=1,\dots, n}|X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\M,n}^*(\P_n)| \;\le\; K^*(\tau, C). $$ Here, $\beta_{\M,n}^*(\P_n)$ is the pseudo parameter from Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudo}.
nodes.statement_short: The linear predictors $X_{i,n}[M]\beta^*_{\M,n}$ at the pseudo parameter are bounded by a constant depending only on $\tau$ and $C$.
assumptions: Suppose that Conditions~\ref{cond:X2}(\ref{cX2:rank},\ref{cX2:Huber}) and \ref{cond:H}(\ref{cH:cdf},\ref{cH:concave}) hold and fix $\tau\in(0,1/4)$.
conclusions: $$ \sup_{\substack{\M\in\mathsf{M}_n\\\P_n\in\mathbf{P}_n^{(\mathrm{bin})}(\tau)}} \max_{i=1,\dots, n}|X_{i,n}[M]\beta_{\M,n}^*(\P_n)| \;\le\; K^*(\tau, C). $$ Here, $\beta_{\M,n}^*(\P_n)$ is the pseudo parameter from Lemma~\ref{lemma:pseudo}.

nodes.name: Lemma D.2
